deep.reconstruction:
The page, titled 'Cellules', sets up an axiomatic, purely topological notion of stratification for Grothendieck's 1974 'topologie modérée' (tame topology) project. The previous page listed further conditions one might add (connected leaves, non-singular leaves, equisingularity) and studied which open subsets inherit them.

Definition I. Let X be a topological space and (F_i)_{i in I} a partition of X into non-empty 'leaves' (feuilles). The partition is called admissible if:
(i) it is locally finite;
(ii) each closure F̄_i is a union of leaves (the frontier condition);
(iii) each F_i is open in F̄_i, i.e. locally closed in X.
The sets F̄_i are called 'closed leaves'.

Injectivity lemma. F̄_i = F̄_j implies F_i = F_j. Suppose F_j ⊂ F̄_i. By the frontier condition, either F_j = F_i or F_j ⊂ F̄_i − F_i. The set F̄_i − F_i is closed because F_i is open in F̄_i. So in the second case F̄_j ⊂ F̄_i − F_i, which is strictly smaller than F̄_i since F_i ≠ ∅. Hence the partition is determined by the family Φ_i = F̄_i.

Axiomatisation II of the closed leaves:
(0) the Φ_i cover X;
(i) the family is locally finite;
(ii) the Φ_i are closed;
(iii) each intersection Φ_i ∩ Φ_j is a union of Φ_k's;
(iv) if Φ_j does not contain Φ_i, then Φ_j (meaning Φ_j ∩ Φ_i) is nowhere dense ('rare') in Φ_i.

Necessity. Φ_i ∩ Φ_j is a union of closed leaves Φ_k ⊊ Φ_i. Each such Φ_k lies in the closed set Φ_i − F_i, which is nowhere dense in Φ_i because F_i is open and dense there.

Sufficiency. Grothendieck sets F_i = Φ_i − ⋃_{Φ_j ⊊ Φ_i} Φ_j.
- Partition: for x in X, the finitely many Φ's containing x have, by (iii), a smallest member. The marginal note says x ∈ F_i exactly when Φ_i is the smallest Φ containing x.
- F_i is locally closed, because a locally finite union of closed sets is closed.
- (F_i) is locally finite.
- F̄_i = Φ_i: by (iv), F_i is the complement of a locally finite union of nowhere-dense closed subsets, hence dense in Φ_i.
- Frontier condition: if x ∈ F_j ∩ Φ_i, then Φ_j is the smallest Φ containing x, so Φ_j ⊂ Φ_i and hence F_j ⊂ Φ_i.

In modern terms, this is the dictionary between locally finite stratifications satisfying the frontier condition and suitable locally finite families of closed sets, the 'closed strata', ordered by inclusion. Equivalently, it is the datum of a continuous map X → (I, ≤) with the Alexandrov topology having locally closed, dense-in-closure fibres. It is a foundational lemma for a theory of 'cells' / tame stratified spaces.
errors: In II, Grothendieck should require the Φ_i to be pairwise distinct and non-empty. Otherwise the reconstructed F_i can coincide for distinct indices, and could be empty if Φ_i = ∅ (density of an empty set is vacuous).
II(iv) is literally written 'Φ_j est rare dans Φ_i'. It must be read as 'Φ_j ∩ Φ_i is nowhere dense in Φ_i', since Φ_j need not lie inside Φ_i.
Density of F_i in Φ_i uses that a locally finite union of closed nowhere-dense subsets of Φ_i is nowhere dense. This holds because locally such a union is a finite union, but it is left implicit.
The uniqueness of a smallest Φ containing x uses (iii) together with distinctness of the Φ's. The argument is sketched only in the marginal note.

ideas.what: Admissible partition: a locally finite partition into locally closed leaves satisfying the frontier condition
ideas.modern_name: Stratification with frontier condition (decomposition à la Whitney/Thom/Mather; poset-stratified space)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney (1965), Thom (1969), Mather (1970); poset-stratified formulation in Lurie HA Appendix A, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 discusses tame stratified structures in general terms; this precise axiomatics is not there as far as I know

ideas.what: Equivalence between the strata and the family of closed strata, with an intrinsic axiomatisation of the latter (cover, locally finite, closed, intersection-closed, nowhere-density)
ideas.modern_name: Closed-strata description of a stratification / continuous map to a poset with Alexandrov topology

ideas.what: Injectivity of the map leaf ↦ closure
ideas.modern_name: Strata determined by their closures under the frontier condition

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful but routine point-set bookkeeping on stratifications satisfying the frontier condition, the standard closed-strata equivalence. It is historically interesting as groundwork for Grothendieck's tame-topology programme, but contains nothing new to a specialist.
transcription_corrections: The page number written at the bottom is 53.
In I, '(0) (F_i) est une partition de X' is an interlinear addition above (i). The crossed-out word after 'loc. finie' is illegible.
II(iv) reads 'Φ_j ⊉ Φ_i … Φ_j est rare dans Φ_i', with a heavily scribbled-out fragment before 'Φ_j'.
The marginal note on the left (attached by a brace to the partition claim) reads roughly: 'x ∈ F_i, savoir i tel que x ∈ Φ_i et Φ_i soit le plus petit de ceux-ci (existe grâce à (i) (iii))'.
